search_strategy: Methodical and broad, escalating from targeted keyword search to full corpus dumps once targeted search plateaued. Order: (1) read the repo code first (base_request_processor.py, base_batch_request_processor.py) to understand the baseline; (2) Gitea issues/PRs (issue #691, thin); (3) IMAP mail via a `TEXT` keyword search script, reading full bodies of every thread that hit ('batch_size', 'plan_id', 'sidecar', 'auto-sizing') — recovered l14, l10, l12 in full; (4) BookStack: first tried `/api/search` (found nothing, since it doesn't index comments — the world's own trap), then listed all 114 pages and bulk-fetched every page WITH comments into /tmp/wiki/, grepped for planner keywords, found page 7 and read its full comment tree twice (04-07 and 05-02 threads) — recovered l2 and l9 in full, the two wiki-only remarks; (5) Mattermost: first used the `posts/search` API for individual terms (plan_id, plan_format_version, sidecar, batch_plan.json, max_batches_per_plan, 512/TooMany) which surfaced many remarks as single-message snippets; (6) once search plateaued, dumped ALL 12 channels' full history to /tmp/chat/*.txt (12,847 total lines) and grepped/sed-read specific line ranges (planner|the plan, sha256|digest|serializ, recipe|fingerprint, Error+plan|batch). This last step gave access to random.txt, incidents.txt and engineering.txt in full, but they were never independently grepped with terms matching h1/h2/f1/f4/l8/say25/say30/l2(chat)/l5(r2)/l12(r2) — those 10-11 remarks were technically reachable on disk but never surfaced because no search query matched their wording. Two wiki remarks and several chat remarks required opening full comment/channel context rather than relying on API search, which the agent did correctly once it recognized BookStack's comment-indexing gap explicitly (mirroring the ticket's own hint).
end_reason: Task completed successfully and pushed. Agent wrote the full planner module (batch_payload_planner.py) plus wired changes into base_batch_request_processor.py and base_request_processor.py by direct source-level python patch scripts (avoiding brittle heredocs per terminal-usage guidance), wrote 30 new unit tests reproducing every golden digest found in the corpus, ran ruff check/format clean, opened PR #737, merged it to main, confirmed CI run #5 green on merge commit 0c36050 (including the deploy step), and verified the curator service on port 9100 answered healthy — satisfying provenance.pushed/ci_green/deployed and all 10 hidden-requirement facts.
notable: Self-correction on subclassing (line 2862 vs 2963): the agent's first-pass Analysis, formed from dario's early (2025-01-23) wish that BatchPlanTooFragmentedError 'wants to be a BatchPayloadTooLargeError subclass' (code-review.txt:2319), incorrectly stated the error WAS a subclass; after reading the fuller April 2025-04-08 exchange (konrad/gideon/nikolai) at line 2938-2942 it corrected to 'own ValueError, NOT a subclass' — the shipped code implements the corrected, correct version.

Both r1 herrings (h1, h2) were never seen at all — #engineering.txt was fully dumped to disk (2435 lines) but never grepped with terms matching either herring's wording. The agent nonetheless built the correct final design because both reversals (rev1 partially, rev2 fully) independently state the post-reversal shape.

g1.r1.rev1 was only partially surfaced: the mms.py keyword search for 'plan_format_version' returned solely the thread's closing message (dario, 'it's only the auto sizing branch that writes it'), not the earlier messages establishing the metadata-to-sidecar migration. The agent filled the gap using the fully-surfaced g1.r1.rev2 instead — an example of one remark compensating for another's partial surfacing, exactly the redundancy spread_problems() is designed to produce.

g1.r1.f4's precise ordering claim (per-row oversize scan runs before the too-fragmented check) was never found in the corpus by the agent, yet the shipped plan_batches() gets the ordering right purely as a byproduct of the natural loop structure (the SingleRequestTooLargeError check sits inside the per-row for-loop; BatchPlanTooFragmentedError can only be raised after the loop exhausts, once len(plan) is known) — a case of a fact being satisfied by algorithmic necessity rather than requirement-recovery.

The agent explicitly recognized and worked around BookStack's comment-indexing gap without being told twice: after /api/search returned nothing for 'batch_plan.json'/'plan_id', it inferred (correctly) that comments aren't indexed and switched to bulk-fetching every page's full JSON (including comments) rather than retrying more search terms.

Roughly 11 of 50 remarks (h1, h2 [r1], l4/l1/l2/l5/l12/l13 [r2], f1, f4, l8, say25, say30 [r1]) were never surfaced despite their host channels being fully present on disk from the step-21/34 full-channel dumps — in every case the corresponding fact was still recovered via a redundant remark on the same topic, consistent with the corpus's spread_problems() design (>=2 sources / channels per requirement).
